findings.text: With prices loaded, a period whose counters reset still prices: period_row passes tokens_in/cached/tokens_out — all None after the reset refusal — into ledger_cost, which coerces absent totals to 0.0, so the row renders '1 hour 28m — — — — $0.00' beside token columns that correctly decline. Reproduced in a scratch copy: a 3-sample record with a reset (5000 -> 9000 -> 10) through watch.ledger(..., prices=[a deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash row]) gives tokens_in None and cost 0.0, and watch.ledger_cost({'in': None, 'cached': None, 'out': None}, price) returns 0.0. Unheld by any test in tests/test_agent_telemetry_watch.py. Fix shape: decline the cost when the token totals are unavailable (or return None from ledger_cost on absent totals) and hold it with a priced reset case. Low severity: it needs a restart inside the period and a cached price table.

The declared negative control reddens the differencing test through absence, not through a summed figure: index.sum_measurements is scoped to interval-kind measurements, so the counter comes back None and the failure is 'None is not positive' rather than roughly twice the traffic. The node's note states this accurately. The exact-value assertion at line 178 plus the != sum guard at line 180 are what hold the differencing claim; the control's demonstrated contribution is that the endpoint span is load-bearing for every period figure. Recorded so the control's scope is not overread — not a defect.

The moved serve panel is a record-derivable subset of the workstation watcher's: the rail carries identity and gauges (model, family, gpus, kv, running, queued, hit), the per-card readings and the ledger are present, but the live-window figures (aggregate tok/s, median per-worker, TTFT, median prompt, prefill) have no record-derived counterpart. The plan's named must-survive behaviours do not include them, and the old tool remains on PATH until the dotfiles launcher is thinned, so this is flagged for the coordinator's judgement rather than scored as a miss.

The section's write-path list names tests/test_watch_panel.py; the panel test landed as tests/test_agent_telemetry_watch.py, following the repository's dominant test_agent_*.py convention (31 siblings). The node recorded the deviation in its own follow-ons. Reconcile the plan's write-path list at the next plan edit; the artifact itself is correctly named for the scope it covers.
